pairs.subject: hitl-approval
pairs.evidence: lib/articles/humanActs.ts:36 The approval record holds only a timestamp and patch ids: there is no decider and no fingerprint of the post that was shown. landing.ts then re-reads post/ from disk at land time, so nothing checks that what lands is what the human approved.

techniques.evidence: lib/articles/humanActs.ts:35 Approve can only leave awaiting-approval; an approve after a reject or a double approve is a loud 409, not a merge. The missing version binding is recorded under decision-records.
lib/articles/humanActs.ts:36 The record has no who and no version or fingerprint of the approved post. A rejection reason is mandatory (humanNote.ts trimmedNote), so the why half does exist.
lib/articles/landing.ts:29 The machine's check and critique cannot produce an admit. Landing requires a recorded human approval.
lib/articles/registryWrite.ts:330 A retried landing whose PR failed reuses the branch already pushed at the recorded commit instead of pushing a second one, so the continuation is idempotent.
lib/articles/registryWrite.ts:307 The landing PR names which dimensions the deterministic check measured and which were left to human judgement, so it is visible where an instrument existed.

lib/articles/mediumPackage.ts:266 The hand path for the Medium post is a prose numbered README (steps 1-4: drag in PNGs in order, swap each table), which is the artifact this technique names as wrong. lib/medium does automate a private draft, but that code is outside this context.
